_notes: What happened on the feast, one line rolled per feast per week and appended to 'X this week.' in the digest. {sacristan}, {usher}, {flowers}, {choir}, {counter}, {widow}, {youth} fill from the parish's cast (systems/cast.ts), or the plain word when nobody holds the part.
epiphany: The chalk went home in envelopes, and by Tuesday three people had asked what the letters meant.
The Magi arrived at the crib on Saturday night, moved by {sacristan}, who had hidden them in the sacristy since Christmas.
The blessing of the homes was announced, and two families asked, which is two more than last year.
santo_nino: The Santo Niño was carried in procession by the Filipino community, and the ten-thirty ran forty minutes long, and nobody minded.
A hundred small images of the Child were blessed at the end of Mass, held up by their owners like tickets.
The hall smelled of lumpia by noon and the choir sang in Tagalog, which the organist had rehearsed for a month.
tet: The Vietnamese community kept the New Year with a Mass for the ancestors and firecrackers on the steps that {usher} tried to stop and then did not.
Red envelopes went to the children after Mass, and one came to the rectory with your name on it.
The altar of the ancestors stood in the hall for the week, with fruit and incense, and the older people bowed to it going past.
candlemas: The candles were blessed in the vestibule and carried in, and the smoke set off nothing, for once.
{sacristan} ordered the year's candles on the strength of the blessing, and the bill came the same week.
A procession in the cold with lit candles, and half of them out by the door.
ash_wednesday: Ashes at seven, noon, and seven, and a line out the door at noon of people you had never seen and will not see until Easter.
The ashes ran out at the noon Mass and {sacristan} burned last year's palms in a coffee can in the parking lot.
A man asked for ashes at the rectory door at nine at night, and got them.
st_joseph: The St. Joseph table went up in the hall, three tiers of bread and fava beans, and the Italian families stood by it like a guard.
A Mass for the fathers of the parish, and a blessing for the men, some of whom had not been blessed in years.
The workers' feast: a plumber and a carpenter read, and did it better than the lectors.
annunciation: The Annunciation on a weekday, kept by the daily Mass crowd and the school, if there is one, and by nobody else.
A Lenten solemnity: the Gloria sung once, strangely, in the middle of the fast.
The flowers were white for the day, and back to bare on Thursday.
palm_sunday: The palms ran out at the ten-thirty and {usher} split the last ones down the middle with his thumbnail.
The Passion read in parts, and the crowd said 'Crucify him' too quietly, as it always does.
Palms woven into crosses by the older women and handed to children who did not know what to do with them.
holy_thursday: Twelve feet washed, one of them belonging to a man who had not been to Mass in years and cried.
The altar stripped after Mass in silence, and the church left dark, and one old man stayed until midnight.
The procession to the altar of repose went around the block, and the neighbours came to their doors.
good_friday: The veneration of the cross took forty minutes, and the line of people kissing the wood did not thin.
The three o'clock service was full; the seven o'clock was the Spanish community's, with the living Stations on the street.
Silence in the church from noon, and the collection for the Holy Land, which was small.
easter_vigil: The fire was lit in the parking lot in a wind and the paschal candle went out twice on the way in.
Four baptized and six received, and the church full of people who had never seen it done.
The Exsultet sung by {choir}, who had practised it for six weeks and got through it.
easter: Every Mass full, and chairs in the aisles, and the ten-thirty starting late because the eight-thirty would not leave.
Lilies on every step, and {flowers} on her knees among them before the first Mass.
The collection was the year's largest and the parking lot the year's worst.
divine_mercy: The Divine Mercy chaplet at three, with the image on the altar and a smaller crowd than the novena had promised.
The Sunday after Easter, and the church back to its size, and the lilies going brown.
Confessions were heard from two o'clock, and a line formed for the first time since Lent.
ascension: The Ascension on a Sunday, as the region keeps it, and the paschal candle put out after the Gospel.
The homily on the going-up, and the children looking at the ceiling.
A first communion class made their communion at the ten-thirty, in white, photographed to distraction.
pentecost: Red vestments, red flowers, and {choir} singing the sequence, badly, with feeling.
The bishop came for confirmations, forty of them, and left before the reception.
The Gospel was read in five languages by five parishioners, and the Vietnamese reader stole it.
corpus_christi: The procession went around the block with the canopy and the monstrance, and a man on a porch took his cap off.
Rose petals scattered by the first communicants in front of the Blessed Sacrament, and a trail of them into the hall.
Benediction at the end, and the Tantum Ergo, and the smell of the incense in your cassock for a week.
sacred_heart: The enthronement of the Sacred Heart in three homes this week, at their asking, with the family kneeling in the living room.
The image was garlanded by {flowers}, and the old devotions had their day.
A Friday feast: the daily Mass crowd and the school, and a quiet Mass with a lot of feeling in it.
sts_peter_paul: The Peter's Pence collection was taken, and {counter} noted that it was smaller than the usual second collection.
The feast of the two apostles, and the homily on the two kinds of priest, which some of them took personally.
Red vestments in June, and the church hot, and the fans on.
assumption: A holy day in the middle of August, and the seven o'clock evening Mass fuller than the morning.
The blessing of herbs and flowers, an old custom that {flowers} revived and nobody understood.
A Marian procession at dusk with the statue on a platform and eight men who found it heavier than last year.
czestochowa: The Polish community's feast, with the icon of the Black Madonna carried in and the hymn sung in Polish by people who had learned it as children.
A pilgrimage to the shrine, two buses, back after dark, with the rosary said on the highway.
Pierogi in the hall and the Polish flag beside the American one, both of them faded.
korean_martyrs: The Korean community kept the martyrs with a Mass in Korean and a lunch that lasted until evening.
The names of the hundred and three read out, and the church quiet for it.
A Korean priest came for the day and preached, and the parish's own community grew for a week.
all_saints: The children came to Mass dressed as saints, and one as a bishop, and one as something nobody could identify.
A holy day on a weekday, with the school Mass full and the evening Mass half full.
The litany of the saints sung, all of it, and the older people knew the responses without the sheet.
all_souls: The book of the dead was open on a stand by the altar and the names in it filled every Mass.
The names of the year's dead read out, and {widow} in the front pew for one of them.
A Mass at the cemetery in the cold, with the graves blessed and the grass wet.
christ_the_king: The last Sunday of the year, and the annual report in the bulletin, and {counter} watching people read it.
The Te Deum sung, or attempted, at the end of the ten-thirty.
A homily on the kingship that {arguer} had a word about on the steps.
advent_start: The wreath blessed and the first candle lit by the youngest family in the parish, who were late.
The church bare and violet, and the Gloria gone, and the choir relieved.
Advent began, and the first person asked when the Christmas Mass schedule would be out.
immaculate_conception: A holy day in Advent with a Mass at noon that the downtown workers came to and left from at twelve forty.
The patronal feast of the country, kept by the daily crowd and a few who remembered.
White vestments in violet season, and the flowers back for a day.
guadalupe: The mañanitas at five in the morning, mariachis in the cold, and the church full before dawn.
Roses at the foot of the image, hundreds of them, and the Aztec dancers in the aisle.
The Guadalupe Mass ran two hours and the tamales in the hall ran out by ten.
simbang_gabi: The nine dawn Masses began, and the Filipino community was in the pews at five each morning with the lights strung on the parols.
Bibingka in the hall after each dawn Mass, and a rice cake left on the rectory step.
The last of the nine Masses was the fullest, and the choir sang in Tagalog and English by turns.
christmas: The midnight Mass was full by eleven-thirty, and the four o'clock vigil fuller, and {usher} stood people along the walls.
The crib was blessed and the Child laid in it by the oldest parishioner, who had to be helped down the step.
Poinsettias on every surface, {flowers} triumphant, and the choir's carols before the Mass.
holy_family: The Sunday in the octave, and the families blessed at the end of Mass, and a couple renewing vows after fifty years.
A quiet Sunday after the feast, with the church still decorated and the people tired.
The homily on the family, which is always a risk, and went well enough.
patronal: The patronal feast: a procession, a novena that ended in it, and a dinner in the hall the committee had planned since spring.
The parish's own day, with the statue carried and the older people singing the hymn the parish sings only once a year.
The bishop sent a letter for the feast, which was read, and a Mass with more of the old parishioners than the new.
